fixes.explanation: True, and they answer together. Moses had set the words before the elders (Exodus 19:7). Then all the people answered together, "We will do everything that the LORD has spoken." (Exodus 19:8) That's a big yes, friend.

The text says they answered with a yes. After Moses sets the words before the elders, all the people answer together, "We will do everything that the LORD has spoken." (Exodus 19:8) Then Moses brought their words back to the LORD.

The text says He does. Once Moses has gone up, the LORD says to him, "Go down and warn the people not to break through to see the LORD, lest many of them perish." (Exodus 19:21) So the card is true, friend. That's the instruction Moses gets at the summit.

Paran isn't the stop in this story, friend. The text says Israel set out from Rephidim and entered the Wilderness of Sinai (Exodus 19:2). That's where they camped in front of the mountain. Good guess, but Sinai is the one.
Zin isn't where this passage lands them. It says they "…entered the Wilderness of Sinai, and Israel camped there in front of the mountain." (Exodus 19:2) Sinai, friend, that's the one to remember.

The third month it is. The text says they came to the Wilderness of Sinai "…on the same day of the month that the Israelites had left the land of Egypt…" (Exodus 19:1) Same day of the month as the day they left. Now THAT is a date worth circling.

Seventh isn't the month the verse gives, friend. The text puts the arrival in the third month, on the same day of the month they left Egypt (Exodus 19:1). Third, not seventh. I'd have to check my calendar twice on that one.

Guests sounds friendly, but the verse says something else. It says "…you will be My treasured possession out of all the nations…" (Exodus 19:5) Possession, friend, and a treasured one at that. Treasured is the kind of word you save for the last cookie in the box.

The text says the opposite of that. The LORD says that if Israel will indeed obey His voice and keep His covenant, they will be His treasured possession out of all the nations, "…for the whole earth is Mine." (Exodus 19:5) So yes, He says the whole earth is His. That's a big line to tuck inside an offer.

The text doesn't mention new leaders at all. It says they must be prepared by the third day, "…for on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people." (Exodus 19:11) The LORD coming down is the whole reason for getting ready.
True. The text says "…whether man or beast, he must not live." (Exodus 13:13 is not it, friend, this is Exodus 19:13.) So the rule about touching the mountain covers animals just like people.

The text says he did tell them. After the people washed their clothes (Exodus 19:14), Moses said to them, "Be prepared for the third day…" (Exodus 19:15) So that instruction comes right after the washing.

Cheering isn't what the text says. It says the thick cloud and the very loud ram's horn came "…so that all the people in the camp trembled." (Exodus 19:16) They trembled, friend. Cheering is a whole different mood.

Singing isn't the word the verse uses. It says the loud blast of the ram's horn went out "…so that all the people in the camp trembled." (Exodus 19:16) Trembling is the word, friend. I bet knees were knocking.

That's the reason the text gives. "Mount Sinai was completely enveloped in smoke, because the LORD had descended on it in fire." (Exodus 19:18) The LORD coming down in fire is the cause the verse names for all that smoke.
A campfire is a cozy picture, and the text doesn't use it. It says, "…the smoke rose like the smoke of a furnace…" (Exodus 19:18) A furnace, friend. That's a much bigger kind of smoke.

That's not what the verse says. It says, "…as the sound of the ram’s horn grew louder and louder, Moses spoke and God answered him in the thunder." (Exodus 19:19) So God answers in the thunder, not in a gentle whisper. Thunder is the word the text uses, friend.

True. After the LORD called Moses to the summit and Moses went up (Exodus 19:20), the LORD said to him, "Go down and warn the people not to break through to see the LORD, lest many of them perish." (Exodus 19:21) Moses has already been up that mountain more than once in this passage, so I bet his legs have opinions.

True. The LORD says, "Even the priests who approach the LORD must consecrate themselves, or the LORD will break out against them." (Exodus 19:22) The priests are named right there in His words. That little word "even" is doing real work.

Aaron, friend. The LORD says, "Go down and bring Aaron with you." (Exodus 19:24) Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). The passage ends with Moses going down and speaking to the people (Exodus 19:25).
Hur isn't named in this passage. The LORD tells Moses, "Go down and bring Aaron with you." (Exodus 19:24) Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). So Aaron's the one the LORD names.
